subject: Weekly Revision
summary: all five topics of Week 6: momentum, flow measurement and dimensional analysis; viscous flow and boundary layer; analytical reasoning; turbulent flow and pipe losses; thermodynamics basics and pure substances (3 questions each)

questions.text: A pitot-static tube is placed at the centre of an air duct. The differential water manometer connected to it reads 40 mm. Taking the density of air as 1.2 kg/m³, the density of water as 1000 kg/m³, the pitot-tube coefficient as 0.98 and g = 9.81 m/s², the air velocity (in m/s, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: A pitot-static tube measures the dynamic pressure Δp = ½ρairV², and V = C√(2Δp/ρair).
Δp = ρ<sub>w</sub>gh = 1000 × 9.81 × 0.040 = 392.4 Pa (the air column in the manometer is negligible)
Exam tip: Use the density of the flowing fluid (air) under the square root, and the manometer liquid only to convert the reading into Δp.

questions.text: The drag on a submarine moving at 2 m/s in sea water is to be found from a 1 : 20 model tested in the same sea water under Reynolds similarity. The ratio of the drag on the model to the drag on the prototype is
solution: Concept: A fully submerged body has no free-surface waves, so viscous forces dominate and Reynolds similarity applies.
Same fluid: V<sub>m</sub>L<sub>m</sub> = V<sub>p</sub>L<sub>p</sub> → V<sub>m</sub> = 20 × 2 = 40 m/s
F ∝ ρV²L², so Fm/Fp = (Vm/Vp)² (Lm/Lp)² = 20² × (1/20)² = 1
Exam tip: Under Reynolds similarity with the same fluid, forces are equal in model and prototype; that is why such model tests need very high speeds or a different fluid.

questions.text: A 30 mm diameter water jet with velocity 25 m/s strikes a fixed, smooth curved vane and is deflected through 150°, as shown. Taking the density of water as 1000 kg/m³ and neglecting friction, the force exerted by the jet on the vane in the direction of the jet (in N, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Momentum equation along the jet axis: F = ṁ(Vin,x − Vout,x). On a smooth fixed vane the speed stays V.
Exam tip: A 180° turn (U-shaped cup, as in a Pelton bucket) gives the maximum, 2ρAV²; a flat plate normal to the jet gives ρAV².

questions.text: A shaft of 80 mm diameter rotates at 1200 rpm in a journal bearing 120 mm long. The radial clearance of 0.1 mm is filled with oil of dynamic viscosity 0.08 Pa·s. Assuming a linear velocity profile in the oil film, the power lost in the bearing (in W, round off to the nearest integer) is ______
solution: Concept: Thin oil film → Couette flow: τ = μU/h. Viscous torque = τ × (πDL) × D/2, power = Tω.
Exam tip: P ∝ μN²D³L/h: doubling the speed quadruples the loss, halving the clearance doubles it.

questions.text: For fully developed laminar flow in a circular pipe, the kinetic-energy correction factor α and the momentum correction factor β are, respectively,
solution: Concept: α = (1/A)∫(u/V)³dA and β = (1/A)∫(u/V)²dA, with the parabolic profile u = 2V(1 − r²/R²).
Integrating gives α = 2 and β = 4/3 ≈ 1.33.
Turbulent profiles are much flatter: α ≈ 1.03–1.1 and β ≈ 1.01–1.04.
Exam tip: Always α > β > 1 for a non-uniform profile; both equal 1 only for uniform flow.

questions.text: A thin flat plate 1.5 m long (in the flow direction) and 0.6 m wide is towed edgewise at 0.2 m/s through still water (density 1000 kg/m³, kinematic viscosity 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m²/s). Using the Blasius result CD = 1.328/√ReL for a laminar boundary layer, the total skin-friction drag on both sides of the plate (in N, round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Check that the boundary layer is laminar (ReL < 5 × 10⁵), then F = CD × ½ρU² × area.
Re<sub>L</sub> = UL/ν = 0.2 × 1.5/10⁻⁶ = 3 × 10⁵ (laminar over the whole plate)
Exam tip: Don't forget the factor 2 for both faces; the local coefficient at x is 0.664/√Rex, exactly half the average coefficient.

questions.text: In a certain code, FLOW is written as GNRA. How is PUMP written in that code?
solution: Concept: Compare letter positions: F→G (+1), L→N (+2), O→R (+3), W→A (+4, wrapping past Z).
Apply the same +1, +2, +3, +4 to PUMP: P→Q, U→W, M→P, P→T
Code = QWPT
Exam tip: Write the alphabet positions (A = 1 … Z = 26) once and count forward; remember to wrap Z → A.

questions.text: Pointing to a girl in a photograph, Ravi says, "She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather." Assuming Ravi's father is that only son, how is the girl related to Ravi?
solution: Concept: Decode the chain from the far end.
The only son of Ravi's grandfather = Ravi's father.
The daughter of Ravi's father = Ravi's sister.
Exam tip: 'Only son' removes uncles from the picture; draw a small family tree with + and − for male and female.

questions.text: In a class of 60 students, 35 study Thermodynamics, 30 study Fluid Mechanics and 12 study neither. The number of students who study both subjects is ______
solution: Concept: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).
Students studying at least one subject = 60 − 12 = 48
Exam tip: Check: only Thermo = 18, only Fluids = 13, both = 17, neither = 12; total 60.

questions.text: A pipeline consists of 600 m of 300 mm diameter pipe followed by 400 m of 200 mm diameter pipe, both with the same friction factor. Neglecting minor losses, the length of a single 250 mm diameter pipe (same friction factor) that gives the same head loss at the same discharge (in m, round off to the nearest integer) is ______
solution: Concept: At fixed Q and f, hf = 8fLQ²/(π²gD⁵) ∝ L/D⁵ (Dupuit's equation for equivalent pipes).
L<sub>e</sub>/D⁵ = L₁/D₁⁵ + L₂/D₂⁵ → L<sub>e</sub> = 600(250/300)⁵ + 400(250/200)⁵
Exam tip: The small-diameter segment dominates: halving D raises the loss 32 times.

questions.text: In turbulent pipe flow the thickness of the viscous sublayer is 0.05 mm, and the average height of the wall roughness is 0.15 mm. According to the usual criterion (smooth if ε/δ′ < 0.25, rough if ε/δ′ > 6), the pipe behaves as
opts: in the transition regime between smooth and rough
questions.ans: (C) in the transition regime between smooth and rough
solution: Concept: Compare the roughness height ε with the viscous-sublayer thickness δ′ = 11.6ν/u*.
ε/δ′ = 0.15/0.05 = 3, which lies between 0.25 and 6.
So the pipe is in the transition regime: f depends on both Re and ε/D (Colebrook).
Exam tip: The same pipe can be smooth at low Re and rough at high Re, because δ′ shrinks as velocity rises.

questions.text: Water flows from a large open tank through a 50 m long, 50 mm diameter horizontal pipe (Darcy f = 0.025) with a sharp-edged entrance (K = 0.5) and discharges as a free jet into the atmosphere, as shown. The water level is 10 m above the pipe centreline. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the discharge (in litres per second, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Energy equation from the free surface to the jet: H = V²/2g (jet) + 0.5V²/2g (entry) + fLV²/(2gD) (friction).
Exam tip: For a free jet, the 1.0 in the bracket is the jet's kinetic energy; for a pipe ending under water, it is the exit loss. The total is the same.

questions.text: On a new temperature scale °N, the ice point is 25 °N and the steam point is 175 °N, with the scale linear in Celsius. The temperature at which the Celsius and °N readings are numerically equal is
solution: Concept: Two linear scales are related by (N − ice)/(steam − ice) on each scale.
Equal readings: t = 25 + 1.5t → t = −50
Exam tip: The zeroth law makes such scales possible: any thermometric property gives a linear scale once two fixed points are chosen. For °C and °F the equal reading is −40.

questions.text: A gas in a piston–cylinder device, restrained by a linear spring, expands so that its pressure varies linearly with volume from 150 kPa at 0.02 m³ to 450 kPa at 0.06 m³. The work done by the gas (in kJ) is ______
solution: Concept: Boundary work W = ∫p dV is the area under the process line on the p–V diagram.
For a straight line the area is a trapezium: W = ½(p₁ + p₂)(V₂ − V₁)
Exam tip: kPa × m³ = kJ. Work and heat are path functions: the same end states joined by a different path give different work.

questions.text: Superheated steam at 10 MPa and 400 °C has a specific volume of 0.02641 m³/kg (from steam tables). Taking the gas constant of steam as 0.4615 kJ/kg·K, the compressibility factor Z of the steam (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Z = pv/(RT) measures the departure from ideal-gas behaviour (Z = 1 for an ideal gas).
So the ideal-gas equation would overpredict the specific volume by about 1/0.85 − 1 ≈ 18 %.
Exam tip: Steam behaves as an ideal gas only at low pressure (roughly below 10 kPa) or very high temperature; near the saturation dome use the tables.
